content: 1. Regularly monitor for signs of respiratory depression and sedation when using fentanyl. Adjust the fentanyl dosage as needed until stable drug effects are achieved. 2. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Both fexinidazole and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid combining fexinidazole with drugs that block potassium channels or further prolong the QT interval. 4. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of finasteride by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 5. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of finerenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium levels during initiation and dosage adjustments of finerenone or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 6. Both fingolimod and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Both flecainide and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 8. Fluconazole significantly increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. Monitor closely if coadministered. 9. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase the risk of hypotension, syncope, and CNS depression. 10. Flucytosine enhances the effects of fluconazole through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 11. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Both fluconazole and fluoxetine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 13. Both fluphenazine and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 14. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of flurbiprofen by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 15. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of fluvastatin by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 16. Both fluvoxamine and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 17. Both fluconazole and formoterol prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 18. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Both fluconazole and foscarnet prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 21. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of fosphenytoin by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Both fluconazole and fostemsavir prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 23. Both gadobenate and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Both gemifloxacin and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Both fluconazole and gemtuzumab prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Fluconazole decreases gentamicin levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 27. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of gepirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Both gepirone and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. 28. Both gilteritinib and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Coadministration is contraindicated. 29. Both fluconazole and givinostat prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at initiation, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or increases by more than 60 ms from baseline. 30. Both fluconazole and glasdegib prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc prolongation. 31. Fluconazole increases glimepiride levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Fluconazole increases glipizide levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Fluconazole increases glyburide levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong CYP2C9 inhibitors may further decrease glyburide metabolism. 34. Goserelin increases fluconazole toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 35. Both granisetron and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Fluconazole increases guanfacine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dosage to half the recommended dose if coadministered. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 37. Both fluconazole and haloperidol prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 38. Histrelin increases fluconazole toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 39. Fluconazole increases hydrocortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Both hydroxychloroquine sulfate and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 41. Fluconazole increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Both hydroxyzine and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Fluconazole increases ibrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., anti-infectives for ≤7 days), interrupt ibrutinib therapy until the inhibitor is discontinued. 44. Fluconazole increases ibuprofen levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 45. Fluconazole increases ibuprofen IV levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 46. Both fluconazole and ibutilide prolong the QTc interval. Coadministration is contraindicated. 47. Fluconazole decreases ifosfamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors may reduce ifosfamide metabolism, potentially decreasing its therapeutic effects. 48. Fluconazole increases iloperidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both fluconazole and iloperidone prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 49. Fluconazole increases imatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 50. Fluconazole increases imipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both fluconazole and imipramine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 51. Both indacaterol (inhaled) and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 52. Both fluconazole and indapamide prolong the QTc interval. Coadministration is contraindicated. 53. Fluconazole increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Fluconazole increases infigratinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 55. Both inotuzumab and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiation, and monitor periodically during treatment. 56. Fluconazole increases irinotecan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Fluconazole increases irinotecan liposomal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Fluconazole increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Both isoflurane and fluconazole prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 60. Fluconazole increases isradipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 61. Both fluconazole and itraconazole prolong the QTc interval. Fluconazole also increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 62. Fluconazole increases ivabradine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid combining ivabradine with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 63. Fluconazole increases ivacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the ivacaftor dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product guidelines for precise dosage adjustments. 64. Fluconazole increases ivosidenib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase ivosidenib plasma concentrations, raising the risk of QTc prolongation. Both fluconazole and ivosidenib prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 65. Fluconazole increases ixabepilone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Both fluconazole and ketoconazole prolong the QTc interval. Fluconazole also increases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 67. Fluconazole increases kola nut levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 68. Fluconazole increases lacosamide levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when coadministered with strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 69. Fluconazole increases lansoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 70. Fluconazole increases lapatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both fluconazole and lapatinib prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 71. Fluconazole increases lefamulin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both fluconazole and lefamulin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 72. Fluconazole increases lemborexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Avoid combining lemborexant with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors. 73. Both fluconazole and lenvatinib prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. 74. Fluconazole increases lesinurad levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 75. Leuprolide increases fluconazole toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 76. Fluconazole increases levamlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with moderate and strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema to determine the need for dose adjustment. 77. Both fluconazole and levofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 78. Both fluconazole and levoketoconazole prolong the QTc interval. Fluconazole also increases levoketoconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised.
